reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Godly and June and The Jackal at the Ram-Fight (Book I); combining the two pages is disclosed and no plot event is invented.

The monk is a sympathetic, unnamed ಸನ್ಯಾಸಿ; the Shiva and caste teaching, the sacred-thread ceremony and the vow rite are removed with disclosure, and only the conman's piety is shown as false. The ಆಷಾಢಭೂತಿ gloss (a Kannada byword for a hypocrite) is correct.
Age band 10+: the rams' blood and the jackal's death are told in plain, calm sentences and never drawn; the jackal dies of its own greed.

The theft is revealed only on the monk's return, so the pause question comes first; the reorder is disclosed. Fixed before approval: an ambiguous pronoun in scene 6 now names the monk and says the robe lay on the bank.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text. One generation, no edits.
The monk's patched saffron robe, the red money bundle and Ashadhabhuti's dhoti and shawl are consistent; both men have similar natural skin tones and no thread, tilak, ash marks, tuft or beads.
The ram fight shows two clean heads meeting with no blood; the jackal is small and far away and unhurt in panel 4 and absent from panel 5. Panel 6 shows the empty robe and footprints leading away.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
